Done. The fix is in `/tmp/pi-max-mid2/T-30-naive-datetime-compare-1/work/tokens/tokens.py`.

## What changed

In `is_expired()`, I added a check that detects naive datetimes (no `tzinfo`) and attaches UTC to them, treating naive inputs as UTC — consistent with the service-wide tz-aware UTC timezone. The comparison then works without raising `TypeError`.

```python
def is_expired(token: dict, at: datetime) -> bool:
    """Return True if the token is expired at `at`.

    Naive datetimes are treated as UTC, matching the tz-aware
    service-wide timezone, so naive inputs never break the comparison.
    """
    if at.tzinfo is None:
        at = at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return at >= token["expires_at"]
```

`issue()` was left completely unchanged, as required.

## Verification

Tested with both naive and aware inputs:

| Input | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Naive before expiry (treated as UTC 11:30, expiry 13:00) | `False` ✓ |
| Naive at expiry (13:00) | `True` ✓ |
| Naive after expiry (14:00) | `True` ✓ |
| Aware UTC before expiry | `False` ✓ |
| Aware EST at expiry | `True` ✓ (cross-TZ aware comparisons still work) |
| `issue()` output | unchanged — still tz-aware UTC ✓ |

The old code would have raised `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` for naive inputs (confirmed by the test), and the new code handles all cases correctly.
